'''Isezuka Kofun''' (伊勢塚古墳) is an ancient [[kofun]] located in {{ill|Kamiochiai, Fujioka, Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県藤岡市上落合|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiochiai, Fujioka, Gunma Prefecture|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. It is part of the {{ill|Shiroishi Kofun Group|ja|白石古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiroishi Kofun Group|qq=}} and is designated a Historic Site by Gunma Prefecture.
== Overview ==
The Isezuka Kofun is situated on the lowest terrace of a three-level river terrace typeed along the right bank of the Kabura River in southern Gunma Prefecture. Multiple archaeological investigations have been conducted at the site.
The mound is an irregular octagon, measuring 27.2 meters in diameter and 6 meters in height{{Sfn|Isezuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. The mound consists of four tiers, with the lowest tier being polygonal (irregular octagon) and the udder tiers being circular{{Sfn|Isezuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. The mound’s surface is covered with {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|qid=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi|1=Fukiishi}}, and cylindrical, humanoid, and shield-shaped {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|qid=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}} were found on the second tier{{Sfn|Isezuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}. The burial chamber is a double-sleeved {{ill|yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening southward. It is the largest stone chamber in Fujioka City and is notable for its distinctive "pattern masonry" construction and dome-shaped ceiling{{Sfn|Isezuka Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}. burial goods such as {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|qid=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery|1=Sue pottery}} have been discovered. The mound is estimated to have been built in the late {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}} (late 6th century){{Sfn|Isezuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}} or the latter half of the 6th century<ref name="Description Board">Historic Site description board.</ref>.
The site was designated a Gunma Prefecture Historic Site in 1973 (Shōwa 48)<ref name="Gunma Prefecture"/>. It has since been preserved and made accessible to the public.
== Historical Timeline ==
* {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=1938|1=Shōwa era}} (Shōwa 13): Listed in the ''Jōmō Kofun Sōran'' as "Midori Village Tomb No. 56."
* {{ill|1973|en|1973|qid=Q2477|lt=Showa 48|1=1973}}: Designated a Gunma Prefecture Historic Site on August 21<ref name="Gunma Prefecture"/>.
* {{ill|1987|en|1987|qid=Q2429|lt=Showa 62|1=1987}}: Survey conducted, confirming the mound’s octagonal type (reported by Fujioka City Board of Education in 1988){{Sfn|Isezuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}.
* {{ill|1997|en|1997|qid=Q2088|lt=Heisei 9|1=1997}}: Survey conducted to confirm the area (Fujioka City Board of Education){{Sfn|Isezuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}.
* {{ill|1998|en|1998|qid=Q2089|lt=Heisei 10|1=1998}}: Additional survey conducted (Fujioka City Board of Education){{Sfn|Isezuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}.
== Burial Chamber ==
[[File:Isezuka Kofun (Fujioka), 3D-B-2.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Overview of the stone chamber}}]]
[[File:Isezuka Kofun (Fujioka), 3D-N-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Stone chamber diagram}}]]
The burial facility consists of a double-sleeved {{ill|yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens southward. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Isezuka Kofun (Zoku Kofun)|2002}}:
* Total length: 8.9 meters
* burial chamber: Length 4.7 meters, rear wall width 1.84 meters, central width 2.41 meters, front width 1.54 meters
* Passage: Length 4.24 meters
The stone chamber features unique "pattern masonry," where quartzite cobbles and schist slabs are arranged vertically. The chamber has a domed ceiling, and its cross-section is hourglass-shaped<ref name="Description Board"/>. The ceiling stones consist of two rounded sandstone pieces, and the rear wall is similarly made of sandstone{{Sfn|Isezuka Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}. The entry portal is constructed with schist slabs, including a pseudo-lintel{{Sfn|Isezuka Kofun (Kofun)|1989}}.
